translations.answer: Maintainer pointed out that the original code forgot to normalize the configuration. The model uses continuous joints, parameterized as [cos(theta), sin(theta)], so normalization should be applied before ABA, and the returned value must be re-assigned to q. The thread did not provide the corrected acceleration output or revert to a full walking model retest, so this can only be considered as a confirmed input correction, and not as a resolution to the complete swing leg issue.
translations.applicability: Applies to the configuration vector of Pinocchio continuous joints and their ABA/constraintDynamics calls; the full robot still needs to be checked for other dynamics inputs.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Original author simplified from walking constraintDynamics to a single pendulum ABA and provided Python code and URDF.
translations.details.attempts.1: Maintainer provided a complete script snippet with q = pin.normalize(model, q).
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Check URDF joint type and model.nq/model.nv; continuous joints cannot be filled with a single scalar angle directly.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Normalize q before calling ABA/constraintDynamics, and retain the returned value.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Use q = pin.normalize(model, q) to receive the normalized value, then call pin.aba; do not only call normalize and discard the return value.
translations.details.environments.0: pinocchio3-preview, Python, attachment single_pendulum.urdf; original post did not provide OS, specific commit, or build options.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread did not provide the original author's normalized -4.905 reference, nor revert to a full walking/constraintDynamics model retest, so the complete swing leg issue still needs to be verified separately.
translations.details.limits.1: This card cannot attribute all large accelerations to configuration normalization; inertial, units, external forces, and constraints also need independent verification.
translations.details.limits.2: The attached code/URDF was not re-run in the current environment.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Maintainer identified the issue as unnormalized configuration, explained that continuous joints are parameterized as [cos(theta), sin(theta)], and the original author did not publish the corrected values.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why should we check continuous-joint configuration normalization when the ABA gives an acceleration larger than the analytical expectation?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before real-time WBC, check if the configuration manifold is valid and has finite values; large accelerations should not be directly converted to torque.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Maintainer pointed out that the original q was not normalized; the continuous joint uses [cos(theta), sin(theta)] parameterization.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Single pendulum length 2, mass 1, moment of inertia 1, gravity 9.81, center of mass to pivot distance 1; at pi/2 zero velocity initialization, original author expected -4.905, but ABA gave -7.7.
translations.details.symptoms.1: In a larger walking model, the original author first observed swing-leg joint accelerations that were too large and inconsistent with other solvers.
translations.source.locator: Pinocchio #1534 comment 934651753 provides the normalize script; comment 973980396 explains the continuous joint parameterization; comment 974012875 emphasizes receiving the return value.
translations.source.title: Pinocchio continuous joint configuration normalization causes ABA acceleration mismatch
